t: Lesson 9 — Step 7: capping and the cap feeder
html:
In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 9 is this chapter: it checks that this lesson’s tags are made, that S7_Cap exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • Start the line: the green column lamp on the capper lights
  • A bottle is capped

Same shape as the fill, plus the cap supply. Add the JSR above JSR(S3_Index) and write:

Tags this lesson needs

Create these before you type the rungs (Verify reports any you miss as unknown). Tags from earlier lessons are not repeated.

TagTypeKindDescription
Cap_DoneBOOLbase tagLatched when the ram has been down; cleared when the belt steps
Cap_PresentBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.15Capper CapPresent: a cap is waiting at the chuck
Cap_RamBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.9LogixPro O:2/9 · Cap ram
Cap_LowBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.14Capper CapLow: the chute is down to its low count
Cap_FeederBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.10Capper Feeder: runs the vibratory cap bowl, refilling the chute
Cap_Fill_TTIMERbase tagCap feeder run-on after CapLow clears
Cap_GreenBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.11Capper green indicator (column)
Cap_AmberBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.12Capper amber indicator (column)

The rungs

How it fits together

Rungs 0–3 mirror the fill station: a whole bottle under the head (Exist 10, not Broken 8), a cap waiting (Cap_Present), not yet capped → Cap_Req; the head comes down; LS7 at the bottom of the stroke latches Cap_Done; the belt stepping clears it. The Broken bit matters here: a head that comes down on a broken bottle crushes it (try it, below). Rungs 4–5 are the cap feeder: when the chute runs low, Cap_Feeder starts the magazine and seals in; once Cap_Low clears, the run-on timer gives it eight more seconds (about 24 caps) and then the seal-in breaks. Rungs 6–7 drive the two lights on the column: green while running with caps in the chute, amber while cycling or low.

Run it

Start the line. At stop 10 the head comes down on each filled bottle and presses a cap on, and the magazine turns one pocket per cap; the green column lamp is on. The bottles still leave at the end of the line, broken ones included, which step 8 will fix.

Try it

Set the Capper’s caps in the chute at start to 3, run the line, and watch the amber lamp, the feeder rung and the magazine spin as the chute refills. Then take XIO(Broken[0].8) out of rung 0 and watch what the head does to a broken bottle.

rungs.head: S7_Cap · Rung 0
rungs.comment: CAP REQUEST: after the shift, Exist bit 10 is the bottle under the chuck and Broken bit 8 says it is whole; it has not been capped, and a cap is waiting (Cap_Present). A broken bottle gets no cap: the chuck would only crush it. With the chute empty the request never comes and the bottle goes on uncapped: watch the amber light
rungs.words: When Exist[0].10 (Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher) is on, Broken[0].8 (Broken bottle (LogixPro B3:30). During the dwell: filler 4, capper 7, scrap gate 11, divert gate 18; after the shift one bit higher) is off, Dwell.DN (the done bit of Dwell: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle) is on, Cap_Done (Latched when the ram has been down; cleared when the belt steps) is off, Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is off, Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on and Cap_Present (Capper CapPresent: a cap is waiting at the chuck) is on, the rung turns Cap_Req (A bottle stands under the cap ram and has not been capped) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Exist[0].10) Examine If Closed asks: true when Exist[0].10 is on.
  2. XIO(Broken[0].8) Examine If Open asks: true when Broken[0].8 is off.
  3. XIC(Dwell.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dwell.DN is on.
  4. XIO(Cap_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Cap_Done is off.
  5. XIO(Conv_Index) Examine If Open asks: true when Conv_Index is off.
  6. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  7. XIC(Cap_Present) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Present is on.
  8. OTE(Cap_Req) Output Energize does: turns Cap_Req on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S7_Cap · Rung 1
rungs.comment: Head down while requested. The capper presses the cap on at the bottom of the stroke

pred.q: Cap_Req is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cap_Ram is on.

rungs.words: When Cap_Req (A bottle stands under the cap ram and has not been capped) is on, the rung turns Cap_Ram (LogixPro O:2/9 · Cap ram) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cap_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Req is on.
  2. OTE(Cap_Ram) Output Energize does: turns Cap_Ram on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S7_Cap · Rung 2
rungs.comment: Head at the bottom (LS7): latch Cap_Done, which drops Cap_Req and lifts the head

pred.q: Cap_Req is off and LS7 is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cap_Done is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Cap_Req).

rungs.words: When Cap_Req (A bottle stands under the cap ram and has not been capped) is on and LS7 (LogixPro I:1/12 · Cap ram down) is on, the rung latches Cap_Done (Latched when the ram has been down; cleared when the belt steps) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cap_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Req is on.
  2. XIC(LS7) Examine If Closed asks: true when LS7 is on.
  3. OTL(Cap_Done) Output Latch does: latches Cap_Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cap_Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: S7_Cap · Rung 3
rungs.comment: The belt is stepping: the next bottle is uncapped
rungs.words: When Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is on, the rung unlatches Cap_Done (Latched when the ram has been down; cleared when the belt steps).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Conv_Index) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conv_Index is on.
  2. OTU(Cap_Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cap_Done. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cap_Done when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S7_Cap · Rung 4
rungs.comment: CAP FEEDER: start the bowl when the chute runs low and seal in; the run-on timer below stops it once the chute has filled past the low float

pred.q: Cap_Low is on, Cap_Feeder is off, Cap_Fill_T.DN is off and Line_Run is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cap_Feeder is on.

rungs.words: When either (Cap_Low (Capper CapLow: the chute is down to its low count) is on) or (Cap_Feeder (Capper Feeder: runs the vibratory cap bowl, refilling the chute) is on), Cap_Fill_T.DN (the done bit of Cap_Fill_T: Cap feeder run-on after CapLow clears) is off and Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, the rung turns Cap_Feeder on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Cap_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Low is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cap_Feeder) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Feeder is on.
  2. XIO(Cap_Fill_T.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when Cap_Fill_T.DN is off.
  3. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  4. OTE(Cap_Feeder) Output Energize does: turns Cap_Feeder on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Cap_Feeder on, and Cap_Feeder’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: S7_Cap · Rung 5
rungs.comment: RUN-ON: once CapLow clears, keep feeding 8 s more (about 24 caps at 3 caps/s), then the seal-in breaks
rungs.words: When Cap_Feeder (Capper Feeder: runs the vibratory cap bowl, refilling the chute) is on and Cap_Low (Capper CapLow: the chute is down to its low count) is off, the rung runs the timer Cap_Fill_T (Cap feeder run-on after CapLow clears) toward 8000 ms (8 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cap_Feeder) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Feeder is on.
  2. XIO(Cap_Low) Examine If Open asks: true when Cap_Low is off.
  3. TON(Cap_Fill_T,8000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Cap_Fill_T toward 8000 ms (8 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Cap_Fill_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: S7_Cap · Rung 6
rungs.comment: GREEN LIGHT on the capper column: running with caps in the chute

pred.q: Line_Run is on, Cap_Present is off and Cap_Low is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cap_Green is off. It stops at XIC(Cap_Present).

rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, Cap_Present (Capper CapPresent: a cap is waiting at the chuck) is on and Cap_Low (Capper CapLow: the chute is down to its low count) is off, the rung turns Cap_Green (Capper green indicator (column)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIC(Cap_Present) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Present is on.
  3. XIO(Cap_Low) Examine If Open asks: true when Cap_Low is off.
  4. OTE(Cap_Green) Output Energize does: turns Cap_Green on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S7_Cap · Rung 7
rungs.comment: AMBER LIGHT: the head is cycling, or the chute is low. Try it: set Caps in the chute at start to 3 on the Capper and watch the feeder rung take over
rungs.words: When either (Cap_Req (A bottle stands under the cap ram and has not been capped) is on) or (Cap_Low (Capper CapLow: the chute is down to its low count) is on), the rung turns Cap_Amber (Capper amber indicator (column)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Cap_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Req is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cap_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cap_Low is on.
  2. OTE(Cap_Amber) Output Energize does: turns Cap_Amber on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Exist.desc: Bottle present, one bit per stop (LogixPro B3:10). During the dwell: filler 6, capper 9, scrap gate 13, divert gate 20; after the shift (Dwell.DN) one bit higher

Broken.desc: Broken bottle (LogixPro B3:30). During the dwell: filler 4, capper 7, scrap gate 11, divert gate 18; after the shift one bit higher

Dwell.desc: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle

Cap_Done.desc: Latched when the ram has been down; cleared when the belt steps

Conv_Index.desc: Latched while the belt steps one pitch

Cap_Present.desc: Capper CapPresent: a cap is waiting at the chuck

Cap_Req.desc: A bottle stands under the cap ram and has not been capped

Cap_Low.desc: Capper CapLow: the chute is down to its low count

Cap_Feeder.desc: Capper Feeder: runs the vibratory cap bowl, refilling the chute

Cap_Fill_T.desc: Cap feeder run-on after CapLow clears
